findings.where: First screen, the lead paragraph and the row of topic pills under the heading (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The first screen shows nothing a visitor can check. It names no body he has worked for, no role, no year, no region and no legal background. The only standing is self-description: the lead says whom he advises, and five keyword pills repeat the same words (Development banks, Governments) without adding any evidence.
findings.who_objects: A development bank's procurement officer who arrives from LinkedIn. They select advisors by relevant experience, project type and region. On this screen they cannot tell this man from any PPP consultant, so they leave to check elsewhere before writing.

findings.fault: The page never says where he works or where he is based. Nothing names a region, country or the places of his talks, so the 5-second test's "where" is left blank.
findings.who_objects: Agency staff whose terms of reference name a region. They need to see that he has worked in their part of the world before they get in touch.

findings.where: First screen, the heading "In my view, we are at a turning point in the story of public-private partnerships."
findings.fault: The heading claims a turning point but never says what it is. Neither the lead nor anything else on the screen explains it, and nothing links to the piece the sentence comes from. Taken alone, the line reads like a generic thought-leadership slogan rather than a view the visitor can follow up.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor who reads the heading first. It raises a question that the page leaves unanswered, so the line's promise of insight comes to nothing.

findings.where: Article specimen, the PDF row "Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge · Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF"
findings.fault: The lecture is listed with no venue or host, so the one dated piece of work on the page cannot be checked and shows no one who invited him.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader judging his standing by who asked him to speak. Without the venue, the strongest proof on the page is lost.

findings.where: First screen, the outlined topic pills (PPP Law, Infrastructure, Development banks, Governments, Risk allocation) on the hatched blue field with the ghost "PPP" behind the heading
findings.fault: Keyword pills over a striped field with a watermark are the stock dressing of a consultancy or software landing page. They make the first screen look like a template any firm could own, not a personal advisor's page.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose test fails "a look any consultancy could own" and anything slick. Bank staff also expect a lawyer-advisor's page to be sober, not dressed in marketing chips.

findings.where: Phone, the first screen (top 844 px of phone-01)
findings.fault: On a phone, the first screen holds only the header, the photograph and the heading. The line saying what he does and the email action both fall below the first screen, so it has no action on it.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who opens the link from LinkedIn on a phone. They see a face and an opinion, but not what he offers or how to reach him, unless they scroll.
